title: Starlight Pilot Onboarding: Deployment Roadmap and Evaluation Checklist
body:
OVERVIEW

Customer: Starlight HealthTech (internal alias: starlight)
Primary contact: Aisha Bello, Head of ML Platform
Pilot objective: Validate Redwood Dedicated as the production inference path for Starlight’s clinical note summarization pipeline (SentiSummarize). Run a 4-week, low-risk deployment that demonstrates latency, cost, and fidelity targets on a realistic slice of production traffic.

GOALS & SUCCESS CRITERIA (high-level)
- Business goal: Reduce manual summarization backlog by 70% for ambulatory notes within pilot scope by end of trial.
- Technical goals (pass/fail):
  - Latency: p50 < 120ms and p99 < 800ms for 1.2k token prompts at 90% of observed daily qps.
  - Throughput: sustain 100 concurrent request slots with autoscale burst to 200 without degradation to p90 latency beyond 1.5x baseline.
  - Cost: average inference spend <= $30 per 1M tokens processed (end-to-end including retry overhead).
  - Quality: evaluated rubric score >= 4.2/5 on 300 blind clinical notes vs. current human-assisted summaries (metrics: factuality, completeness, redaction safety).
  - Security & compliance: no PHI leakage in telemetry logs stored outside customer VPC, KMS enabled and verified.

ACCEPTANCE MATRIX (Must / Should / Nice-to-have)
- Must (blocker if unmet):
  1) Canary route with automatic fallback to smaller model on capacity issues.
  2) Nightly regression alerts triggered by eval harness if average rubric drops > 0.25 points.
  3) Signed data handling agreement and KMS key rotation documented in Console.

- Should (pilot success if most met):
  1) Cost target reached within 20% margin of estimate.
  2) Latency SLOs met for >95% of daytime traffic.
  3) Full traceability from request->response (trace id) visible in Console with token-level timing.

- Nice-to-have:
  1) Embedding-based similarity cache reduces repeated same-note requests by >30%.
  2) Basic reranking pipeline integrated to de-duplicate summaries.

TECHNICAL ASSUMPTIONS
- Customer will provide a 6-hour rolling sample of anonymized clinical notes for initial bench and 300-note evaluation set.
- Network: VPN to Starlight VPC is provisioned ahead of week 1; egress bandwidth >= 200 Mbps measured.
- Models: Start with open-source 13B variant recommended by Redwood catalog; quantized float16 on Dedicated.
- Secrets: Customer KMS key created and accessible to Redwood Private control plane for pilot.

DEPLOYMENT PLAN & TIMELINE (4 weeks)
- Week 0 (prep): sign data agreement, enable KMS, create pilot project in Console, share sample data.
- Week 1 (bench & canary): baseline bench on dev region; deploy canary route for 5% traffic; run smoke tests and latency load tests (10k synthetic reqs).
- Week 2 (scale & integration): integrate with Starlight ingestion worker, enable autoscale policy, verify KV/prefix caching behavior with synthetic repeated prompts.
- Week 3 (validation): run blind eval set, collect rubric scores and logs, iterate prompt/template adjustments.
- Week 4 (wrap & handoff): produce pilot report, review cost forecasts, decision meeting for Dedicated purchase or private on-prem plan.

WORKSHOP AGENDA (Kickoff workshop, 90 minutes)
1) Introductions & objectives (10m)
2) Walkthrough of SentiSummarize call flow (15m)
3) Security & compliance checklist review (10m)
4) Console demo: model catalog, canary config, rollouts (20m)
5) Integration tasks & responsibilities (15m)
6) Runbook: incidents & rollback, escalation path (10m)
7) Q&A and next steps (10m)

RESPONSIBILITIES (RACI-lite)
- Redwood (solutions-engineering): deployment templates, autoscale tuning, eval harness setup, run small-load stress tests.
- Starlight (ML infra): provide anonymized sample set, provision VPC link, validate KMS access, integrate ingestion worker.
- Customer success (Redwood): weekly sync, billing estimate reconciliation, support window setup.

VALIDATION TESTS & EVALUATION CHECKLIST (concrete steps)
1) Latency smoke: run k6 load test (script: k6/starlight-latency.js) at 20 rps for 10 minutes, capture p50/p90/p99.
2) Throughput ramp: synthetic parallel clients increase from 10->200 concurrent and observe autoscale events in Console.
3) Cost sanity: sample 1000 requests, measure token counts and cost report export from Console; compare to estimate.
4) Quality eval: run eval harness (evals/starlight/clinical-rubric.py) against 300 notes; export scored CSV and Slack summary.
5) Telemetry audit: confirm no raw PHI present in logs outside customer VPC; check retention policy.

ROLLBACK & Fallback STRATEGY
- Canary route should be default; auto-fallback to smaller quantized model or to synchronous human-in-loop queue if quality dips below threshold.
- Incident runbook:
  - Severity 1 (site-wide degradation): Roll traffic to fallback variant, page on-call SRE, notify customer success.
  - Severity 2 (degraded perf): Increase instance pool, lower batch sizes, escalate to infra team.

RISKS & OPEN QUESTIONS
- Risk: Real-world note length distribution heavier than sample; may push p99 beyond SLO. Mitigation: measure distribution week 0 and pre-warm KV cache.
- Open question: Is Starlight comfortable with embeddings cache residing in Redwood-managed Redis in Dedicated or must it be customer-hosted?
- Risk: Third-party connector used by Starlight may add 50-200ms upstream latency. Need to isolate in test harness.

NOTES FROM PRE-KICKOFF CALL (summary)
- Starlight runs peak ingestion between 02:00–06:00 UTC, team requests pilot daytime window mapping.
- Priority metrics: factuality and PHI redaction > raw latency for earliest acceptance.
- Customer requests ability to pin model micro-version during pilot for deterministic evals.

NEXT STEPS (immediate)
- Redwood: provision pilot project and send Console invite (action: Maya).
- Starlight: deliver anonymized 6-hour sample and create KMS key (action: Aisha).
- Schedule week 0 prep call within 3 business days.

ATTACHMENTS / ARTIFACTS TO PREPARE
- smoke-test k6 script: k6/starlight-latency.js (repo link in linked_artifacts)
- Eval harness: evals/starlight/clinical-rubric.py
- Sample template for anonymization (attached in Confluence page)

END OF DOCUMENT
